A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original hyperparameter-sensitivity experiments, surrogate-selection evaluations, and subset-fraction analyses in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A and C.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds empirical assumption checks, WikiText2/GPT2 surrogate evaluations, and downstream data-removal results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 still selects the candidate regularization value whose average surrogate indicator is closest to 0.5. The attribution procedures and projection formulations are retained; expanded notation and explanations do not change the algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix C.5 adds an actual downstream data-selection/removal task on MNIST, CIFAR-2, and MAESTRO, extending evaluation beyond LDS. No new dataset is introduced: WikiText2/GPT2, including its language-modeling setting, already appeared in v1.

E2.justification: The new downstream comparisons include random removal and explicit default-regularization IFFIM/TRAK comparisons against their selected-regularization variants, alongside a full-data reference. The original sensitivity-study methods and spectral-quantile selection baselines are retained.

E3.justification: The downstream evaluation introduces removal rates of 10%, 30%, and 50%, using test accuracy for MNIST/CIFAR-2 and test loss for MAESTRO. New assumption checks use projection dimension 4096 and epsilon_g = 0.5. These are added protocols; the original LDS evaluation using 50 independently retrained models remains unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Appendix B.4 adds empirical checks of Assumptions B.7 and B.9 on CIFAR-2 and MAESTRO, estimating their constants relative to the smallest eigenvalue. Figure 7 also extends regularization-sensitivity diagnostics to IFFIM and LoGra on WikiText2/GPT2. The existing subset-fraction robustness analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Appendix C.5 and Tables 2–4 introduce ten-seed experiments reported as means and standard errors. v1's LDS retrainings did not provide this uncertainty-reporting practice. This does not establish increased repetitions for retained experiments, and no formal significance test is specified.

E6.justification: v2 adds assumption-check measurements, Figure 7's LDS curves, and downstream results in Tables 2–4. For example, at 30% MNIST removal, TRAK Selected yields 83.84% accuracy versus 87.92% for TRAK Default; lower accuracy indicates stronger attribution. CIFAR-2 IFFIM Selected and Default have identical reported results. Original Figures 1–6 retain their results.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds an assumption and derivation connecting the alpha weights to leave-one-out effects. Proposition B.8 restores a missing factor of n, propagated into the constants and inequalities in Lemma B.15's proof. The main sufficient-condition theorem and qualitative monotonicity result remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: identifying costly hyperparameter tuning, characterizing sensitivity, and proposing theoretically motivated selection without retraining. The added conclusion sentence about checkpoint sensitivity restates a finding already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds a geometric explanation involving gradient directions, interprets the new constant estimates as support for assumptions in nonconvex settings, and suggests dataset redundancy explains limited effects from 10% removal. The original limitations concerning regularization-specific theory and reliance on LDS remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B.4 documents projected-FIM diagonalization and gradient-based estimation for the new assumption checks. Appendix D changes the listed repository location from the data-attribution-hp organization to TRAIS-Lab. Existing hardware, timing, and default-hyperparameter disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Deng et al.'s 2025 data-attribution survey as reference 9 and cites it in the introduction. The remaining references largely match after renumbering, and the main novelty positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4 separates problem formulation from analysis, introduces notation before the theorem, and adds intuition and a proof sketch. Appendix subsections are expanded and renumbered, with local wording and conference-footer updates. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-panel Figure 7 and three downstream-result tables. Existing Figures 1–6 retain their displays, with local relocation, including placing Figures 2 and 3 together. Table 1's caption moves above the table.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens practical validation beyond v1's LDS-only evaluation through ten-seed downstream experiments across three settings. It also repairs a proof-bound error and adds empirical scrutiny of theoretical assumptions. These address important evidential and mathematical weaknesses. The gains remain qualified: CIFAR-2 shows no IFFIM improvement, and the significance claims lack a specified formal test.
